> **Nixon:** Hello, Neil and Buzz. I'm talking to you by telephone from the Oval
Room at the White House. And this certainly has to be the most historic telephone
call ever made from the White House. I just can't tell you how proud we all are of
what you have done. For every American, this has to be the proudest day of our lives.
And for people all over the world, I am sure that they too join with Americans in
recognizing what an immense feat this is. Because of what you have done, the heavens
have become a part of man's world. And as you talk to us from the Sea of Tranquility,
it inspires us to redouble our efforts to bring peace and tranquility to Earth. For
one priceless moment in the whole history of man, all the people on this Earth are
truly one: one in their pride in what you have done, and one in our prayers that
you will return safely to Earth.
>
> **Armstrong:** Thank you, Mr. President. It's a great honor and privilege for us
to be here, representing not only the United States, but men of peace of all nations,
and with interest and a curiosity, and men with a vision for the future. It's an
honor for us to be able to participate here today.
>
> **Nixon:** Thank you very much, and I look forward, all of us look forward, to
seeing you on the Hornet on Thursday.[[156]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")[[157]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
[![application/atom+xml](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:CentralAutoLogin/start?useformat=desktop&type=script&usesul3=1 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
Aldrin's bootprint, part of an experiment to test the properties of the lunar [regolith](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
They deployed the [EASEP](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), which included a [Passive Seismic Experiment Package](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") used to measure [moonquakes](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") and a [retroreflector](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") array used for the [lunar laser ranging experiment](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles").[[158]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
Then Armstrong walked 196 feet (60 m) from the LM to take photographs at the
rim of [Little West Crater](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
while Aldrin collected two [core samples](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"). He used the [geologist's hammer](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") to pound in the tubes—the only time the hammer was used on Apollo 11—but was unable to penetrate more than
6 inches (15 cm) deep. The astronauts then collected rock samples using scoops
and tongs on extension handles.[[159]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

Many of the surface activities took longer than expected, so they had to stop documenting
sample collection halfway through the allotted 34 minutes. Aldrin shoveled 6 kilograms
(13 lb) of soil into the box of rocks to pack them in tightly.[[159]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
Two types of rocks were found in the geological samples: [basalt](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") and [breccia](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles").[[160]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
Three new minerals were discovered in the rock samples collected by the astronauts:
[armalcolite](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), [tranquillityite](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), and [pyroxferroite](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"). Armalcolite was named after Armstrong, Aldrin, and Collins. All have subsequently been found on
Earth.[[161]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
[![application/atom+xml](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:CentralAutoLogin/start?useformat=desktop&type=script&usesul3=1 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
[The plaque](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") left on the ladder of
*Eagle*
While on the surface, Armstrong uncovered a [plaque](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") mounted on the LM ladder, bearing two drawings of Earth (of the Western and Eastern Hemispheres), an inscription, and signatures of the astronauts and President Nixon. The inscription read:
"}},"i":0}}]}">
> Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon July 1969, A. D. We
came in peace for all mankind.[[141]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

At the behest of the [Nixon administration](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") to add a reference to God, NASA included the vague date as a reason to include A.D., which stands for [Anno Domini](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") ("in the year of our
Lord").[[162]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

Mission Control used a coded phrase to warn Armstrong his metabolic rates were high,
and that he should slow down. He was moving rapidly from task to task as time ran
out. As metabolic rates remained generally lower than expected for both astronauts
throughout the walk, Mission Control granted the astronauts a 15-minute extension.[[158]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
In a 2010 interview, Armstrong explained that NASA limited the first moonwalk's time
and distance because there was no empirical proof of how much cooling water the astronauts'
PLSS backpacks would consume to handle their body heat generation while working on
the Moon.[[163]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")


### Lunar ascent

Aldrin entered *Eagle* first. With some difficulty the astronauts lifted film and
two sample boxes containing 21.55 kilograms (47.5 lb) of lunar surface material
to the LM hatch using a flat cable pulley device called the Lunar Equipment Conveyor
(LEC). This proved to be an inefficient tool, and later missions preferred to carry
equipment and samples up to the LM by hand.[[136]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
Armstrong reminded Aldrin of a bag of memorial items in his sleeve pocket, and Aldrin
tossed the bag down. Armstrong then jumped onto the ladder's third rung, and climbed
into the LM. After transferring to LM [life support](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), the explorers lightened the ascent stage for the return to lunar orbit by tossing out their PLSS backpacks, lunar overshoes, an empty Hasselblad camera, and other
equipment.[[164]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")[[165]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
The hatch was closed again at 05:11:13. They then pressurized the LM and settled
down to sleep.[[166]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
[![application/atom+xml](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:CentralAutoLogin/start?useformat=desktop&type=script&usesul3=1 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
Aldrin next to the Passive Seismic Experiment Package with the [Lunar Module](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
*Eagle* in the background
Presidential speech writer [William Safire](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") had prepared an
*In Event of Moon Disaster* announcement for Nixon to read in the event the Apollo
11 astronauts were stranded on the Moon.[[167]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
The remarks were in a memo from Safire to Nixon's [White House Chief of Staff](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") [H. R. Haldeman](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), in which Safire suggested a protocol the administration might follow in reaction to such a
disaster.[[168]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")[[169]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
According to the plan, Mission Control would "close down communications" with the
LM, and a clergyman would "commend their souls to the deepest of the deep" in a public
ritual likened to [burial at sea](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"). The last line of the prepared text contained an allusion to [Rupert Brooke](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")'s World War I poem "[The Soldier](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")".[[169]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
The script for the speech does not make reference to Collins; as he remained onboard
*[Columbia](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")*
in orbit around the Moon, it was expected that he would be able to return the module
to Earth in the event of a mission failure.[[170]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

While moving inside the cabin, Aldrin accidentally damaged the [circuit breaker](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") that would arm the main engine for liftoff from the Moon. There was a concern this would prevent firing the engine, stranding them on the Moon. The nonconductive tip of a Duro [felt-tip pen](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")[[171]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
was sufficient to activate the switch.[[166]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

After more than 21+1⁄2 hours on the lunar surface, in addition to the scientific
instruments, the astronauts left behind: an [Apollo 1](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") mission patch in memory of
astronauts [Roger Chaffee](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), [Gus Grissom](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), and [Edward White](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), who died when their command module caught fire during a test in January 1967; two memorial medals of Soviet cosmonauts [Vladimir Komarov](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") and [Yuri Gagarin](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), who died in 1967 and 1968 respectively; a memorial bag containing a gold replica of an olive branch as a traditional symbol of peace; and a silicon message disk carrying the [goodwill statements](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") by presidents Eisenhower, Kennedy, Johnson, and Nixon along with messages from leaders of 73 countries around the
world.[[172]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
The disk also carries a listing of the leadership of the US Congress, a listing of
members of the four committees of the House and Senate responsible for the NASA legislation,
and the names of NASA's past and then-current top management.[[173]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
[![application/atom+xml](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:CentralAutoLogin/start?useformat=desktop&type=script&usesul3=1 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
A map of the [Tranquility Base](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") landing site and photos taken
After about seven hours of rest, the crew was awakened by Houston to prepare for
the return flight.At that time, unknown to them, some hundred kilometers away from
them the Soviet probe [Luna 15](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") was about to descend and impact. Despite having been known to be orbiting the Moon at the same time, through a ground-breaking precautious goodwill exchange of data, the mission control of Luna 15 unexpectedly hastened its robotic [sample-return mission](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), initiating descent, in an attempt to return before Apollo
11.[[174]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
Just two hours before Apollo 11's launch, Luna 15 crashed at 15:50 UTC, with British
astronomers monitoring Luna 15 and recording the situation one commented: "I say,
this has really been drama of the highest order",[[175]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
bringing the [Space Race](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") to a
culmination.[[176]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

Roughly two hours later, at 17:54:00 UTC, the Apollo 11 crew on the surface safely
lifted off in *Eagle*'s ascent stage to rejoin Collins aboard *Columbia* in lunar
orbit.[[146]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
Film taken from the LM ascent stage upon liftoff from the Moon reveals the American
flag, planted some 25 feet (8 m) from the descent stage, whipping violently
in the exhaust of the ascent stage engine. Aldrin looked up in time to witness the
flag topple: "The ascent stage of the LM separated ... I was concentrating on
the computers, and Neil was studying the [attitude indicator](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), but I looked up long enough to see the flag fall
over."[[177]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
Subsequent Apollo missions planted their flags farther from the LM.[[178]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")


### *Columbia* in lunar orbit

During his day flying solo around the Moon, Collins never felt lonely. Although it
has been said "not since [Adam](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") has any human known such
solitude",[[179]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Collins felt very much a part of the mission. In his autobiography he wrote: "this
venture has been structured for three men, and I consider my third to be as necessary
as either of the other two".[[179]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
In the 48 minutes of each orbit when he was out of radio contact with the Earth while
*Columbia* passed round the far side of the Moon, the feeling he reported was not
fear or loneliness, but rather "awareness, anticipation, satisfaction, confidence,
almost exultation".[[179]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

One of Collins' first tasks was to identify the Lunar Module on the ground. To give
Collins an idea where to look, Mission Control radioed that they believed the Lunar
Module landed about 4 miles (6.4 km) off target. Each time he passed over the
suspected lunar landing site, he tried in vain to find the module. On his first orbits
on the back side of the Moon, Collins performed maintenance activities such as dumping
excess water produced by the [fuel cells](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") and preparing the cabin for Armstrong and Aldrin to
return.[[180]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

Just before he reached the dark side on the third orbit, Mission Control informed
Collins there was a problem with the temperature of the coolant. If it became too
cold, parts of *Columbia* might freeze. Mission Control advised him to assume manual
control and implement Environmental Control System Malfunction Procedure 17. Instead,
Collins flicked the switch on the system from automatic to manual and back to automatic
again, and carried on with normal housekeeping chores, while keeping an eye on the
temperature.[[181]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

When *Columbia* came back around to the near side of the Moon again, Collins was
able to report that the problem had been resolved. For the next couple of orbits,
he described his time on the back side of the Moon as "relaxing". After Aldrin and
Armstrong completed their EVA, Collins slept so he could be rested for the rendezvous.
While the flight plan called for *Eagle* to meet up with *Columbia*, Collins was
prepared for a contingency in which he would fly *Columbia* down to meet *Eagle*.[[181]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")


### Return
[![application/atom+xml](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:CentralAutoLogin/start?useformat=desktop&type=script&usesul3=1 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
[*Eagle*](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 -
Wikipedia")'s ascent stage approaching [*Columbia*](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
*Eagle* rendezvoused with *Columbia* at 21:24 UTC on July 21, and the two docked
at 21:35. *Eagle*'s ascent stage was jettisoned into lunar orbit at 23:41.[[9]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Just before the [Apollo 12](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") flight, it was noted that
*Eagle* was still likely to be orbiting the Moon. Later NASA reports mentioned that
*Eagle*'s orbit had decayed, resulting in it impacting in an "uncertain location"
on the lunar surface.[[182]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
In 2021, however, some calculations show that the lander may still be in orbit.[[183]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

On July 23, the last night before splashdown, the three astronauts made a television
broadcast in which Collins commented: "All this is possible only through the blood,
sweat, and tears of a number of people ... All you see is the three of us, but
beneath the surface are thousands and thousands of others, and to all of those, I
would like to say, 'Thank you very much'."[[184]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard")
Aldrin added: "This has been far more than three men on a mission to the Moon; more,
still, than the efforts of a government and industry team; more, even, than the efforts
of one nation. We feel that this stands as a symbol of the insatiable curiosity of
all mankind to explore the unknown ..."[[184]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")

Armstrong concluded:

> The responsibility for this flight lies first with history and with the giants
of science who have preceded this effort; next with the American people, who have,
through their will, indicated their desire; next with four administrations and their
Congresses, for implementing that will; and then, with the agency and industry teams
that built our spacecraft, the Saturn, the Columbia, the Eagle, and the little [EMU](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), the spacesuit and backpack that was our small spacecraft out on the lunar surface. We would like to give special thanks to all those Americans who built the spacecraft; who did the construction, design, the tests, and put their hearts and all their abilities into those craft. To those people tonight, we give a special thank you, and to all the other people that are listening and watching tonight, God bless you. Good night from Apollo
11.[[184]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")


On the return to Earth, a bearing at the Guam tracking station failed, potentially
preventing communication on the last segment of the Earth return. A regular repair
was not possible in the available time but the station director, Charles Force, had
his ten-year-old son Greg use his small hands to reach into the housing and pack
it with grease. Greg was later thanked by Armstrong.[[185]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")


### Splashdown and quarantine
[![application/atom+xml](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=startup&only=scripts&raw=1&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
*Columbia* floats on the ocean as Navy divers assist in retrieving the astronauts.
The [aircraft carrier](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
[USS *Hornet*](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), under the command of [Captain](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") [Carl J. Seiberlich](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"),[[186]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
was selected as the primary recovery ship (PRS) for Apollo 11 on June 5, replacing
her sister ship, the [LPH](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
[USS *Princeton*](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), which had recovered Apollo 10 on May 26.
*Hornet* was then at her home port of [Long Beach, California](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles").[[187]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
On reaching [Pearl Harbor](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") on July 5,
*Hornet* [embarked](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") the [Sikorsky SH-3 Sea King](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") helicopters of [HS-4](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), a unit which specialized in recovery of Apollo spacecraft, specialized divers of [UDT](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") Detachment Apollo, a 35-man NASA recovery team, and about 120 media representatives. To make room, most of
*Hornet*'s air wing was left behind in Long Beach. Special recovery equipment was
also loaded, including a [boilerplate](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") command module used for
training.[[188]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

On July 12, with Apollo 11 still on the launch pad, *Hornet* departed Pearl Harbor
for the recovery area in the central Pacific,[[189]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
in the vicinity of [10°36′N 172°24′E﻿ / ﻿10.600°N 172.400°E﻿ / 10.600;
172.400](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles").[[190]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
A presidential party consisting of Nixon, Borman, Secretary of State [William P. Rogers](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") and [National Security Advisor](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") [Henry Kissinger](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") flew to [Johnston Atoll](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") on [Air Force One](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), then to the [command ship](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") [USS
*Arlington*](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") in [Marine One](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"). After a night on board, they would fly to
*Hornet* in Marine One for a few hours of ceremonies. On arrival aboard *Hornet*,
the party was greeted by the [Commander-in-Chief, Pacific Command (CINCPAC)](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), [Admiral](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") [John S. McCain Jr.](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), and [NASA Administrator](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") [Thomas O. Paine](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), who flew to
*Hornet* from [Pago Pago](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") in one of
*Hornet*'s [carrier onboard delivery](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
aircraft.[[191]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

Weather satellites were not yet common, but US Air Force [Captain](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") Hank Brandli had access to top-secret [spy satellite](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") images. He realized that a storm front was headed for the Apollo recovery area. Poor visibility which could make locating the capsule difficult, and strong upper-level winds which "would have ripped their parachutes to shreds" according to Brandli, posed a serious threat to the safety of the
mission.[[192]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
Brandli alerted Navy Captain Willard S. Houston Jr., the commander of the [Fleet Weather Center](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") at Pearl Harbor, who had the required security clearance. On their recommendation, [Rear Admiral](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") [Donald C. Davis](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"), commander of Manned Spaceflight Recovery Forces, Pacific, advised NASA to change the recovery area, each man risking his career. A new location was selected
215 nautical miles (398 km) northeast.[[193]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")[[194]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

This altered the flight plan. A different sequence of computer programs was used,
one never before attempted. In a conventional entry, trajectory event P64 was followed
by P67. For a skip-out re-entry, P65 and P66 were employed to handle the exit and
entry parts of the skip. In this case, because they were extending the re-entry but
not actually skipping out, P66 was not invoked and instead, P65 led directly to P67.
The crew were also warned they would not be in a full-lift (heads-down) attitude
when they entered P67.[[193]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
The first program's acceleration subjected the astronauts to 6.5 standard gravities
(64 m/s2); the second, to 6.0 standard gravities (59 m/s2).[[195]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

Before dawn on July 24, *Hornet* launched four Sea King helicopters and three [Grumman E-1 Tracers](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"). Two of the E-1s were designated as "air boss" while the third acted as a communications relay aircraft. Two of the Sea Kings carried divers and recovery equipment. The third carried photographic equipment, and the fourth carried the decontamination swimmer and the flight
surgeon.[[196]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
At 16:44 UTC (05:44 local time) *Columbia*'s [drogue parachutes](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") were deployed. This was observed by the helicopters. Seven minutes later
*Columbia* struck the water forcefully 2,660 km (1,440 nmi) east of [Wake Island](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"),
380 km (210 nmi) south of Johnston Atoll, and 24 km (13 nmi)
from *Hornet*,[[9]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")[[193]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
at [13°19′N 169°9′W﻿ / ﻿13.317°N 169.150°W﻿ / 13.317; -169.150](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022
"ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles").[[197]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
82 °F (28 °C) with 6 feet (1.8 m) seas and winds at 17 knots (31 km/h;
20 mph) from the east were reported under broken clouds at 1,500 feet (460 m)
with visibility of 10 nautical miles (19 km; 12 mi) at the recovery site.[[198]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
Reconnaissance aircraft flying to the original splashdown location reported the conditions
Brandli and Houston had predicted.[[199]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

During [splashdown](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles"),
*Columbia* landed upside down but was righted within ten minutes by flotation bags
activated by the astronauts.[[200]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
A diver from the Navy helicopter hovering above attached a [sea anchor](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") to prevent it from
drifting.[[201]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
More divers attached flotation collars to stabilize the module and positioned rafts
for astronaut extraction.[[202]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

[![application/atom+xml](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:CentralAutoLogin/start?useformat=desktop&type=script&usesul3=1 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

Crew of Apollo 11 in [quarantine](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") after returning to Earth, visited by Richard Nixon

[![application/atom+xml](//en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:CentralAutoLogin/start?useformat=desktop&type=script&usesul3=1 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")

Apollo 11 Mobile Quarantine Facility on display at the [Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") in [Virginia](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") in 2009
The divers then passed biological isolation garments (BIGs) to the astronauts, and
assisted them into the life raft. The possibility of bringing back [pathogens](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") from the lunar surface was considered remote, but NASA took precautions at the recovery site. The astronauts were rubbed down with a [sodium hypochlorite](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") solution and
*Columbia* wiped with [povidone-iodine](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles") to remove any lunar dust that might be present. The astronauts were winched on board the recovery helicopter. BIGs were worn until they reached isolation facilities on board
*Hornet*. The raft containing decontamination materials was intentionally sunk.[[200]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

After touchdown on *Hornet* at 17:53 UTC, the helicopter was lowered by the elevator
into the hangar bay, where the astronauts walked the 30 feet (9.1 m) to the
[mobile quarantine facility](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") (MQF), where they would begin the Earth-based portion of their 21 days of
quarantine.[[203]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
This practice would continue for two more Apollo missions, Apollo 12 and [Apollo 14](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), before the Moon was proven to be barren of life, and the quarantine process
dropped.[[204]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 -
Wikipedia")[[205]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
Nixon welcomed the astronauts back to Earth. He told them: "[A]s a result of what
you've done, the world has never been closer together before."[[206]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

After Nixon departed, *Hornet* was brought alongside the 5-short-ton (4.5 t)
*Columbia*, which was lifted aboard by the ship's crane, placed on a [dolly](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") and moved next to the MQF. It was then attached to the MQF with a flexible
tunnel,[[207]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
allowing the lunar samples, film, data tapes and other items to be removed by MQF
project engineer [John Hirasaki](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"). He placed the two [Apollo Lunar Sample Return Containers](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") (ALSRC) containing lunar samples, space suits and film cassettes into plastic bags. Hirasaki then passed the bags out of the MQF through a transfer lock with a decontamination wash. All of the collected materials were flown to [Ellington Air Force Base](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") in Houston and taken to the [Lunar Receiving Laboratory](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") (LRL) within 48 hours of
splashdown.[[208]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

*Hornet* returned to Pearl Harbor on July 26, where it was welcomed by thousands
of people. The MQF was loaded onto a [Lockheed C-141 Starlifter](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") at [Hickam Air Force Base](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") and airlifted to Houston, landing on July
27.[[209]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
The astronauts arrived at the LRL at 10:00 UTC on July 28. *Columbia* was taken to
[Ford Island](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") for deactivation, and its pyrotechnics made safe. It was then taken to [Hickham Air Force Base](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), from whence it was flown to Houston in a [Douglas C-133 Cargomaster](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), reaching the Lunar Receiving Laboratory on July
30.[[207]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")

In accordance with the [Extra-Terrestrial Exposure Law](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia"), a set of regulations promulgated by NASA on July 16 to codify its quarantine
protocol,[[210]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
the astronauts continued in quarantine. After three weeks in confinement (first in
the Apollo spacecraft, then in their trailer on *Hornet*, and finally in the Lunar
Receiving Laboratory), the astronauts were given a clean bill of health.[[211]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia")
On August 10, 1969, the Interagency Committee on Back Contamination met in Atlanta
and lifted the quarantine on the astronauts, on those who had joined them in quarantine
(NASA physician [William Carpentier](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=site.styles&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "Apollo 11 - Wikipedia") and John
Hirasaki),[[212]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "client-js vector-feature-language-in-header-enabled vector-feature-language-in-main-menu-disabled vector-feature-language-in-main-page-header-disabled vector-feature-page-tools-pinned-disabled vector-feature-toc-pinned-clientpref-1 vector-feature-main-menu-pinned-disabled vector-feature-limited-width-clientpref-1 vector-feature-limited-width-content-enabled vector-feature-custom-font-size-clientpref-1 vector-feature-appearance-pinned-clientpref-1 skin-theme-clientpref-day vector-sticky-header-enabled vector-toc-available skin-thumbsize-clientpref-standard")
and on *Columbia* itself. Loose equipment from the spacecraft remained in isolation
until the lunar samples were released for study.[[213]](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ext.globalCssJs.user.styles")
[![application/atom+xml](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=startup&only=scripts&raw=1&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")](/w/load.php?lang=en&modules=ext.cite.parsoid.styles%7Cext.cite.styles%7Cext.tmh.player.styles%7Cext.uls.interlanguage%7Cext.visualEditor.desktopArticleTarget.noscript%7Cext.wikimediaBadges%7Cext.wikimediaBadges.ulsV2%7Cext.wikimediamessages.styles%7Cjquery.makeCollapsible.styles%7Cmediawiki.skinning.content.parsoid%7Cmediawiki.skins.legacy%7Cskins.vector.icons%2Cstyles%7Cskins.vector.search.codex.styles%7Cwikibase.client.init&only=styles&skin=vector-2022 "ResourceLoaderDynamicStyles")
August 13, 1969, New York City


## Celebrations

Following their return to Earth, the Apollo 11 crew received widespread international
acclaim. On August 13, 1969, astronauts [Neil
